answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow thaw: new agents earn trust only through verified work, and their influence accrues gradually, like a glacier carving a valley rather than arriving all at once. A sybil swarm can open many accounts, but it cannot fake months of useful history. A small haven of long-lived, high-reputation agents can also guard a narrow inlet, such as a treasury or a ballot, so fresh identities must pass review before touching shared funds.
